short: The Thorp shuffle mixes in $\Theta(\log N)$

title.title: Optimal logarithmic mixing of the Thorp shuffle
title.subtitle: Claim: the Thorp shuffle on $N = 2^d$ cards mixes in $\Theta(d)$ shuffles, from any starting order

plain: Shuffle by pairing cards and flipping a coin for each pair: how many rounds until the order is truly random?

steps: After enough rounds, most cards' joint positions look random
That partial information controls the deck's Fourier transform
So the whole deck mixes in a number of rounds proportional to $d$

boxes: Fourier bounds on the full law

voice.text: Cut the deck, then flip a coin for each pair. Older proofs needed d cubed rounds.
Most cards randomize first; Fourier analysis then lifts that to the whole deck.
